To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The use of ICT in education is a complex phenomenon, which is influenced by a range of factors.
the use of ICT in the classroom is not a simple matter.

(a) the use of a particular ICT tool is likely to have an effect on the learning process that is specific to that context; (b) the effect on learning of a particular ICT resource is not necessarily uniform across contexts; and (c) the use of ICT resources is likely to be affected by the context in which the resource is employed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which the contexts of use affect the outcomes in terms of learning and the implications of these for the design and implementation.
the use of technology in education, and with the effects of this use on learning.
the use of information and communications technology (ICT) in educational contexts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

ICT can be an important factor in promoting learning in schools but that the way in which this is achieved will depend on the nature of the technology, the way it is implemented and the nature of the learning context.
there is no conclusive statement.
the use of ICT in education is a very complex and multi-layered phenomenon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ICT is a complex phenomenon that is best understood through a range of different methods.
ICT can be a powerful resource for learning, provided that it is used in a way that fits the context and is supported by a well-designed curriculum.
, in order to make effective use of ICT, it is necessary to consider the contexts of use, and that this requires the use of a range of methods for data collection and analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of ICT in education is not a simple matter.

the design and use of technology needs to take account of its potential to be appropriated for different purposes in different settings, and that this requires a research approach that is sensitive to the interplay between the technology and its context.
the use of technology in education can be understood in relation to the social practices that are embedded in the context in which it is used.
